rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tilka points to the surah's verses; al-kitāb al-mubīn can mean the surah whose signs expose its inimitability and silence the Arabs.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أمرها في إعجاز العرب وتبكيتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verses make their divine rather than human origin clear to anyone who reflects on them.
rows.anchor: أو التي تبين لمن تدبرها أنها من عند الله لا من عند البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, their Arabic makes their meanings clear and unambiguous to Arabs.
rows.anchor: أو الواضحة التي لا تشتبه على العرب معانيها لنزولها بلسانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the surah clarifies what the Jews asked about Joseph; Jewish scholars reportedly told pagan leaders to ask Muhammad why Jacob's family moved from Syria to Egypt and about Joseph.
rows.anchor: روي أن علماء اليهود قالوا لكبراء المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book containing Joseph's story was sent down as an Arabic Qur'an; Qur'an is a generic name applying to the whole revelation or a part of it.
rows.anchor: أنزلنا هذا الكتاب الذي فيه قصة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of its Arabic form is that its audience understand it fully and not confuse its meanings; compare the hypothetical non-Arabic revelation.
rows.anchor: إرادة أن تفهموه وتحيطوا بمعانيه ولا يلتبس عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qaṣaṣ can mean the act of recounting or the narrated account; as an account it is a verbal noun used for its object, like report/news or creation/hunting.
rows.anchor: تقول : قص الحديث يقصه قصصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If qaṣaṣ means recounting, the phrase can make this Qur'an the object of recounting or treat the phrase as an explanatory source phrase with the narrated object omitted.
rows.anchor: أي بإيحائنا إليك هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account is best either in its striking method and style, unmatched by earlier books and histories, or as the most excellent material because of its lessons, subtleties, wisdom, and marvels.
rows.anchor: أن هذا الحديث مقتص في كتب الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it the best story is scoped to its subject field, as one calls someone the best or most learned in a particular art.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه أحسن ما يقتص في بابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaṣaṣ derives from following a trace: the narrator follows what he remembers piece by piece, just as a Qur'an reciter follows one verse after another.
rows.anchor: من قص أثره إذا اتبعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the following clause inna is lightened from the emphatic particle, and the lām distinguishes it from negation; the pronoun before it refers to revelation, and Muhammad had no prior knowledge of the story.
rows.anchor: واللام هي التي تفرق بينها وبين النافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh qāla is an appositional substitute for aḥsan al-qaṣaṣ because the time contains the story, or it is governed by an understood udhkur, remember.
rows.anchor: لأن الوقت مشتمل على القصص وهو المقصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yūsuf is a Hebrew name; if Arabic, its only reason for diptote declension would be properness, so the name's form does not support an Arabic derivation.
rows.anchor: لأنه لو كان عربيا لانصرف لخلوه عن سبب آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even readings Yūsuf and Yūsaf resembling Arabic active or passive imperfect forms do not make the name Arabic: the famous reading establishes its foreign origin, unlike Yunus with three variants.
rows.anchor: الشهادة ، على أن الكلمة أعجمية

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet identifies Joseph as the noble son of four successive noble ancestors: Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham.
rows.anchor: إذا قيل : من الكريم ؟ فقولوا : الكريم ابن الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yā abat is read with three vowelings; its tāʾ is feminine in form but replaces the possessive yāʾ, and pausing changes it to hāʾ.
rows.anchor: تاء تأنيث وقعت عوضا من ياء الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A feminine ending can attach to a masculine noun, and tāʾ can replace the possessive yāʾ because both it and the possessive ending add material at the word's end.
rows.anchor: قولك : حمامة ذكر وشاة ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kasra before the possessive yāʾ shifts onto tāʾ; it remains because tāʾ is a consonant that must be vocalized, unlike a weak yāʾ that may be silent.
rows.anchor: الكسرة التي كانت قبل الياء في قولك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kasra is not the replaced yāʾ, so its coexistence with the substitute tāʾ is not redundant; forms such as yā abatā likewise allow an added ending.
rows.anchor: الياء والكسرة قبلها شيآن والتاء عوض من أحد الشيئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fatḥa reading may preserve the fatḥa after deleting the alif of yā abatā, or use the corresponding yāʾ movement; ḍamma treats the word like a feminine noun ending in tāʾ.
rows.anchor: أما من فتح فقد حذف الألف من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings vocalize the yāʾ in innī raʾaytu and silence the ʿayn in aḥada ʿashar to ease successive vowels in this compound numeral, except twelve to avoid two silent consonants.
rows.anchor: تخفيفا لتوالي المتحركات فيما هو في حكم اسم واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raʾaytu here is a dream vision, not waking sight: the sun, moon, and stars prostrating together in wakefulness would be a great sign known to Jacob and others.
rows.anchor: رأيت من الرؤيا ، لا من الرؤية

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: A Jew asked the Prophet which stars Joseph saw; after Gabriel informed him, the Prophet named eleven stars, and the Jew affirmed the names.
rows.anchor: روى جابر أن يهوديا جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation makes the sun and moon Joseph's parents; another makes them his father and maternal aunt, with the stars representing his brothers.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الشمس والقمر أبواه

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb relates that at age seven Joseph dreamed eleven tall staffs encircled a small staff that leapt up and uprooted them; his father warned him not to tell his brothers.
rows.anchor: وعن وهب أن يوسف رأى وهو ابن سبع سنين أن إحدى عشرة عصا طوالا

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: At twelve, Joseph dreamed the sun, moon, and stars prostrating, and Jacob again told him not to tell his brothers lest they plot; reports place the brothers' arrival forty or eighty years later.
rows.anchor: ثم رأى وهو ابن ثنتي عشرة سنة الشمس والقمر والكواكب تسجد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon are mentioned after the stars to single out their superior distinction, as Gabriel and Michael are singled out after the angels; alternatively, waw means with.
rows.anchor: أخرهما ليعطفهما على الكواكب على طريق الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second raʾaytu is not redundant: it answers Jacob's implied question about how Joseph saw them, namely, prostrating to him.
rows.anchor: إنما هو كلام مستأنف على تقدير سؤال وقع جوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stars are treated as rational beings because they are described with prostration, a trait associated with rational agents; Arabic commonly transfers a thing's ruling through partial resemblance.
rows.anchor: لما وصفها بماهو خاص بالعقلاء وهو السجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob understood the dream to foretell God's raising Joseph to wisdom and prophethood and granting him honor in both worlds like his forebears, so he feared his brothers' envy and aggression.
rows.anchor: عرف يعقوب عليه السلام دلالة الرؤيا على أن يوسف يبلغه الله مبلغا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruʾyā means vision but is restricted to dreams, unlike ruʾya for waking sight; feminine endings distinguish them as in qurba and qurba.
rows.anchor: إلا أنها مختصة بما كان منها في المنام دون اليقظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings include ruʾyāk with hamza changed to wāw, and ri yāk forms with assimilation and rāʾ vowel variation; the latter are weak because wāw is effectively hamza and does not assimilate, like it does not in ittazara and ittajara.
rows.anchor: وهي ضعيفة ؛ لأن الواو في تقدير الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fayakīdū is subjunctive after an understood an: if Joseph tells them, they will plot against him.
rows.anchor: منصوب بإضمار ( أن ) والمعنى : إن قصصتها عليهم كادوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in yakīdū laka instead of a direct object embeds a verb that governs lām, adding its meaning and intensifying the threat, as in yaḥtālū laka; the verbal noun further emphasizes it.
rows.anchor: ضمن معنى فعل يتعدى باللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's manifest enmity is shown by what he did to Adam and Eve and his vow to lie in wait on God's straight path, so he incites every plot and evil.
rows.anchor: ظاهر العداوة لما فعل بآدم وحواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God chose Joseph for a momentous dream signaling honor and greatness, so He will choose him for great affairs; the teaching clause is independent of the simile.
rows.anchor: كما اجتباك لمثل هذه الرؤيا العظيمة الدالة على شرف وعز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijtibāʾ means selection, from gathering something for oneself, like collecting water in a basin.
rows.anchor: الاصطفاء ، افتعال من جبيت الشيء إذا حصلته لنفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥādīth can mean dreams, which may arise from the self, an angel, or Satan; their taʾwīl is interpretation, and Joseph was the most capable interpreter.
rows.anchor: لأن الرؤيا إما حديث نفس أو ملك أو شيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, taʾwīl al-aḥādīth means explaining divine books, prophetic practice, and their obscure purposes and wisdom; they are called reports because they are transmitted from God and His messengers.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بتأويل الأحاديث معاني كتب الله وسنن الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completion of blessing can mean joining worldly blessing to afterlife blessing, making the family prophets and kings in this world before their high ranks in Paradise.
rows.anchor: ومعنى إتمام النعمة عليهم أنه وصل لهم نعمة الدنيا بنعمة الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Abraham's blessing was friendship with God and rescue from fire and sacrificing his son; Isaac was rescued from sacrifice and Jacob and the tribes came from his line.
rows.anchor: أتمها على إبراهيم بالخلة ، والإنجاء من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says Jacob inferred from the stars' light that Joseph and his brothers would all be prophets, explaining the reference to Jacob's family.
rows.anchor: علم يعقوب أن يوسف يكون نبيا وإخوته أنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers reportedly became jealous after hearing Joseph's dream and complained that even their parents would bow to him.
rows.anchor: لما بلغت الرؤيا إخوة يوسف حسدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Jacob already favored Joseph for youth and promising signs, embracing him constantly; the dream intensified that affection and the brothers' envy.
rows.anchor: كان يعقوب مؤثرا له بزيادة المحبة والشفقة لصغره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob reportedly told Joseph his vision was a scattered matter that God would gather together after a long time.
rows.anchor: لما قص رؤياه على يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āl Yaʿqūb means his household and descendants; āl derives from ahl, as its diminutive shows, and is reserved for people of status rather than ordinary trades.
rows.anchor: آل يعقوب . أهله وهم نسله وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two forefathers are Jacob's grandfather and great-grandfather, treated as fathers because of their precedence; Ibrāhīm and Isḥāq are explanatory apposition.
rows.anchor: وأراد بالأبوين : الجد ، وأبا الجد ؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows who merits election, and in wisdom completes blessing only for someone deserving it.
rows.anchor: لا يتم نعمته إلا على من يستحقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's story contains signs and proofs of God's power and wisdom for those asking about it.
rows.anchor: علامات ودلائل على قدرة الله وحكمته في كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the story proves Muhammad's prophethood to Jews who asked about Joseph because he gave an accurate account without hearing it or reading a book.
rows.anchor: وقيل آيات على نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم للذين سألوه من اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A singular reading āya is reported, and some codices read ʿibra, lesson.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض المصاحف : عبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God told the Prophet about Joseph and his brothers' wrongdoing to comfort him after seeing his own people wrong him.
rows.anchor: إنما قص الله تعالى على النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account names Joseph's brothers and says the first seven were Leah's children, four came from Zilpah and Bilhah, and Rachel later bore Benjamin and Joseph.
rows.anchor: وقيل أساميهم : يهوذا : وروبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in la-Yūsufu is an emphatic lām of initiation, confirming that their claim about their father's greater love is certain.
rows.anchor: اللام للابتداء . وفيها تأكيد وتحقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His brother is Benjamin; although all were brothers, Joseph and Benjamin are singled out because they shared one mother.
rows.anchor: هو بنيامين . وإنما قالوا أخوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥabbu has the singular form for two because the elative with min does not mark number or gender; with the definite article distinction is required, while possessive construction permits either.
rows.anchor: لأن أفعل من لا يفرق فيه بين الواحد وما فوقه ، ولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-naḥnu ʿuṣba is circumstantial: they argue ten capable men deserve more love than two small boys who offer no help or benefit.
rows.anchor: يعني : أنه يفضلهما في المحبة علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their charge of manifest error means Jacob has departed from the correct judgment in preferring the two boys.
rows.anchor: في ذهاب عن طريق الصواب في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUṣba or ʿiṣāba means ten or more; another view extends it to forty, because such a group binds together affairs and withstands adversity.
rows.anchor: العشرة فصاعدا . وقيل : إلى الأربعين

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Al-Nazzāl ibn Sabra transmits from ʿAlī a reading with ʿuṣbatan in the accusative, understood as we gather as a band.
rows.anchor: النزال بن سبرة عن علي رضي الله عنه : ( ونحن عصبة )

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī compares the ellipsis to the Arabic saying that the ʿĀmirī only his aunt, meaning he tends to his aunt.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن الأنباري هذا كما تقول العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order to kill continues the brothers' earlier discussion; they all assented except the one who then says not to kill Joseph.
rows.anchor: من جملة ما حكى بعد قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report names Simeon as the proposed killer; another names Dan, while the rest consented and are therefore collectively described as issuing the order.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الآمر بالقتل شمعون ، وقيل : دان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arḍan is an indefinite, unknown, distant land, with no location or description; it is accusative as an ambiguous place adverb.
rows.anchor: مجهولة بعيدة من العمران ، وهو معنى تنكيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yakhlu lakum wajh abīkum means their father will turn fully toward them; face pictures his attention, or means his person, as in the cited verse, or being free of concern for Joseph.
rows.anchor: يقبل عليكم إقبالة واحدة لا يلتفت عنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After him can mean after Joseph is killed or exiled, or can refer back to the act of killing or casting him away.
rows.anchor: من بعد يوسف ، أي من بعد كفايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣāliḥīn can mean repenting to God for their crime, repairing matters with their father through an excuse, or making worldly affairs run smoothly after Joseph is gone.
rows.anchor: تائبين إلى الله مما جنيتم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takūnū is either jussive coordinated with yakhlu or subjunctive after an implied an, with waw meaning together with, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: منصوب بإضمار أن والواو بمعنى مع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker who proposes not killing Joseph is Judah, the brother with the best opinion of him; he called killing a grave matter.
rows.anchor: هو يهوذا ، وكان أحسنهم فيه رأيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayābat al-jubb is the well's hidden depth, unseen by an observer and dark toward its bottom.
rows.anchor: وهي غوره وما غاب منه عن عين الناظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Munkhil's verse uses ghiyābat for the grave in which a person is buried, supporting the sense of hidden depth.
rows.anchor:
قال المنخل :
وإن أنا يوما غيبتني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings include ghiyābāt in the plural, a doubled form, and ghayba from al-Jaḥdarī.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( غيابات ) على الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jubb is an unlined well, named from the root for digging into earth.
rows.anchor: والجب : البئر لم تطو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaltaqiṭuhu means a traveler passing along the road will pick him up; a reading with feminine taltaqiṭuhu treats baʿḍ al-sayyāra as grammatically feminine.
rows.anchor: بعض الأقوام الذين يسيرون في الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine agreement is like Arabic expressions in which a collective or part is feminine, illustrated by the line about blood reddening the channel's breast and by saying some fingers were lost.
rows.anchor: لأن بعض السيارة سيارة ، كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they are intent on acting to achieve their purpose, this proposal is the right plan.
rows.anchor: إن كنتم على أن تفعلوا ما يحصل به غرضكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers read the two nūns in taʾmannā distinctly or assimilated, with or without nasal coloring; another reading assimilates after a kasra on tāʾ.
rows.anchor: بإظهار النونين ، وبالإدغام بإشمام وبغير إشمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question means why does Jacob fear them when they want good for Joseph, love and pity him, and have shown nothing against trust; the plea tries to dislodge Jacob from his guarded habit and shows he sensed grounds for suspicion.
rows.anchor: لم تخافنا عليه ونحن نريد له الخير ونحبه ونشفق عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nartaʿ means to range freely and eat fruit and other things; the root conveys abundance and spaciousness.
rows.anchor: نتسع في أكل الفواكه وغيرها

rows.speaker: العلاء بن سيابة
rows.claim: Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Sayāba reads yartaʿ with kasra on ʿayn and yalʿab in the nominative.
rows.anchor: العلاء بن سيابة : يرتع بكسر العين ، ويلعب ، بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob could permit their play because it meant racing and spear practice to build strength for fighting, not idle amusement; they call their later race play because it looked like play.
rows.anchor: كان لعبهم الاستباق والانتضال . ليضروا أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call the exercise play because it takes the outward form of play.
rows.anchor: وإنما سموه لعبا لأنه في صورته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in layuḥzinunī is an emphatic lām, like the one in the cited verse, and is one of Sibawayh's causes of similarity.
rows.anchor: اللام لام الابتداء ، كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob gives two reasons: separation from Joseph grieves him because he cannot bear even an hour apart, and a wolf might attack while the brothers are distracted by grazing or play.
rows.anchor: اعتذر إليهم بشيئين ، أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Jacob had dreamed a wolf attacked Joseph, so he warned them; the proverb says calamity is attached to what one says.
rows.anchor: رأى في النوم أن الذئب قد شد على يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dhiʾb is read with hamza in its original form or with it lightened; another etymology links it to wind arriving from every direction.
rows.anchor: بالهمزة على الأصل وبالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath is omitted but understood as by God; the lām introduces the oath, and the oath response suffices instead of a separate conditional response, with the clause about being a band circumstantial.
rows.anchor: القسم محذوف تقديره : والله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They swear that if a wolf takes their brother while ten men are present, they would be losers: ruined by weakness, deserving destruction for uselessness, or deserving a curse of ruin for failing to protect him.
rows.anchor: حلفوا له لئن كان ما خافه من خطفة الذئب أخاهم من بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that they would lose their livestock if they could not protect even one brother.
rows.anchor: إن لم نقدر على حفظ بعضنا فقد هلكت مواشنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob had offered two excuses, but they answer only the wolf concern because his grief at separation angered them and they deliberately ignored it.
rows.anchor: هو الذي كان يغيظهم ويذيقهم الأمرين فأعاروه آذانا صما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An yajʿalūhu is the object of ajmaʿū, meaning they resolved on the affair; a reading has ghiyābāt in the plural.
rows.anchor: مفعول { أجمعوا } من قولك : أجمع الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accounts place the well in Jerusalem, Jordan, between Egypt and Midian, or three farsakhs from Jacob's home.
rows.anchor: هو بئر بيت المقدس . وقيل : بأرض الأردن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted answer to when they took him includes their abuse: they mocked and beat Joseph, refused his pleas, and nearly killed him; Judah invoked their pledge, then stopped them from crushing him at the well.
rows.anchor: فقد روي أنهم لما برزوا به إلى البرية أظهروا له العدواة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They stripped Joseph and his shirt, which they intended to stain with blood to deceive Jacob; Joseph begged for it to cover himself before they lowered him into the well.
rows.anchor: وإنما نزعوه ليلطخوه بالدم ويحتالوا به على أبيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the shirt came from Paradise: Gabriel clothed Abraham in it in the fire, Abraham passed it to Isaac then Jacob, and Gabriel later retrieved and dressed Joseph in it.
rows.anchor: أن إبراهيم عليه السلام حين ألقي في النار وجرد عن ثيابه أتاه جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say revelation came to Joseph in childhood, like John and Jesus; others say he was mature, and al-Ḥasan gives his age as seventeen.
rows.anchor: أوحي إليه في الصغر كما أوحي إلى يحيى وعيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation comforts Joseph in darkness and loneliness, promises his eventual escape, and tells him he will recount his brothers' deed to them.
rows.anchor: أوحي إليه ليؤنس في الظلمة والوحشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not recognize him because of his elevated rank and changed circumstances after a long time; when they later seek provisions he knows them and recounts what they did.
rows.anchor: عن أوهامهم ، ولطول العهد المبدل للهيئات والأشكال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with nun, lanunabbiʾannahum, makes the statement a threat against the brothers; the clause about their not knowing attaches only to the revelation.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( لننبئنهم ) بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A caravan traveling from Midian to Egypt arrived three days after Joseph entered the well, having missed the road and stopped nearby; the isolated well served shepherds, and its salty water became sweet when Joseph was cast in.
rows.anchor: رفقة تسير من قبل مدين إلى مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They sent Malik ibn Dhuʿar al-Khuzaʿi to seek water; a wārid is the person who goes to water to draw for the group.
rows.anchor: رجلا يقال له مالك ابن ذعر الخزاعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yā bushrā is a call to good news, as if inviting it to arrive; readings add the speaker's possessive yāʾ or use yāʾ instead of alif, a known dialect of the Sarawāt.
rows.anchor: نادى البشرى ، كأنه يقول : تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ's yā bushray with sukūn is judged irregular because of two successive sukūns except in a pause.
rows.anchor: وعن نافع : يا بشراي بالسكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Joseph grabbed the bucket rope and emerged as an exceptionally handsome boy; another says the waterman carried him near the caravan and shouted to announce him.
rows.anchor: تعلق يوسف بالحبل ، فلما خرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in asarrūhu may refer to the waterman and his companions hiding Joseph from the caravan, or hiding how they found him and claiming water sellers gave him to them for sale.
rows.anchor: الضمير للوارد وأصحابه : أخفوه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the pronoun refers to Joseph's brothers: they claimed he was their runaway slave and sold him, while he stayed silent for fear they would kill him.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن الضمير لإخوة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biḍāʿatan is an accusative state: they concealed him as trade goods; biḍāʿa is wealth set aside for commerce.
rows.anchor: نصب على الحال ، أي : أخفوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what they do: this warns the men who treated Joseph as merchandise that did not belong to them, or the brothers for their mistreatment of father and brother.
rows.anchor: لم يخف عليه أسرارهم ، وهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sharawhu means they sold Joseph for a conspicuously deficient price, or for clipped, underweight coins.
rows.anchor: مبخوس ناقص عن القيمة نقصانا ظاهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The payment was dirhams rather than dinars; maʿdūda means few coins counted rather than weighed, since only sums of forty or more were weighed, or because large sums defy counting.
rows.anchor: قليلة تعد عدا ولا توزن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the price was twenty dirhams.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : كانت عشرين درهما

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī reports that the price was twenty-two dirhams.
rows.anchor: درهما . وعن السدي : اثنين وعشرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were indifferent to Joseph, accepting a low price because they had merely found him and feared a rightful claimant might take him away.
rows.anchor: ممن يرغب عما في يده فيبيعه بما طف من الثمن لأنهم التقطوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the caravan bought Joseph from his brothers and was indifferent because it believed he was a runaway and feared risking its own property.
rows.anchor: معنى { وشروه } واشتروه ، يعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fīhi is explanatory rather than governed by al-zāhidīn; a prepositional complement cannot precede its governing noun, and it answers what they disdained.
rows.anchor: ليس من صلة { الزهدين } لأن الصلة لا تتقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The buyer, Qitfir or Aṭfir, was the Aziz who held Egypt's storehouses; king Rayyān ibn al-Walīd, an Amalekite, believed in Joseph and died while Joseph lived, followed by Qābūs ibn Muṣʿab, who rejected Joseph's call to Islam.
rows.anchor: قيل هو قطفير أو أطفير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says the Pharaoh of Moses ruled in Joseph's time and lived four hundred years, citing the verse that Joseph came with clear proofs; another says Moses' Pharaoh descended from Joseph's Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: كان الملك في أيامه فرعون موسى ، عاش أربعمائة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph was bought at seventeen, stayed in the household thirteen years, became vizier at thirty, received knowledge and wisdom at thirty-three, and died at 120.
rows.anchor: واشتراه العزيز وهو ابن سبع عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report gives the price as twenty dinars, shoes, and two white garments; another says bidding reached his weight in musk, silver, and silk before Qitfir bought him.
rows.anchor: اشتراه العزيز بعشرين دينارا وزوجي نعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akramī mathwāhu means make his home and stay honorable and pleasant; care for him with kindness so he feels at ease, as the phrase is used of a host's treatment.
rows.anchor: اجعلي منزله ومقامه عندنا كريما ، أي حسنا مرضيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in li-imraʾatihi is governed by qāla, not by the verb bought.
rows.anchor: واللام في { لامرأته } متعلقة يقال ، لا باشتراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He hoped Joseph's training and sound judgment would help with their affairs through competence and trustworthiness, or that they would adopt him as a son because Qitfir was childless.
rows.anchor: لعله إذا تدرب وراض الأمور وفهم مجاريها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three people are called especially perceptive: the Aziz about Joseph, Moses' prospective employer's daughter about Moses, and Abū Bakr when appointing ʿUmar.
rows.anchor: أفرس الناس ثلاثة : العزيز حين تفرس في يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Aziz asked Joseph about himself; Joseph gave his lineage, which the Aziz recognized.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه سأله عن نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kadhālika refers to the rescue and the Aziz's softened heart: in the same way God established Joseph in Egypt and gave him authority to act there.
rows.anchor: الإشارة إلى ما تقدم من إنجائه وعطف قلب العزيز عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rescue and empowerment served the ultimate purpose of teaching Joseph beneficial knowledge and action through interpretation of reports.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك الإنجاء والتمكين لأن غرضنا ليس إلا ما تحمد عاقبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is dominant over His own affair, beyond anyone's obstruction, or over Joseph's affair, directing it Himself despite his brothers' contrary plan.
rows.anchor: على أمر نفسه : لا يمنع عما يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people fail to know that all affairs are in God's hands.
rows.anchor: أن الأمر كله بيد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥudd means ages eighteen, twenty, thirty-three, or forty; its upper limit is also said to be sixty-two.
rows.anchor: قيل في الأشد : ثماني عشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥukm can mean wisdom, knowledge joined to practice and avoidance of ignorance, or judgment among people and jurisprudence.
rows.anchor: حكمة وهو العلم بالعمل واجتناب ما يجهل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about rewarding doers signals Joseph's piety and excellence in his youth; God granted him judgment and knowledge in recompense for that excellence.
rows.anchor: تنبيه على أنه كان محسنا في عمله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says whoever worships God well in youth is granted wisdom by God in maturity.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : من أحسن عبادة ربه في شبيبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Murāwada is a reciprocal form from rāda, to come and go: she maneuvered deceptively to obtain what he did not want to surrender, a euphemism for attempted intercourse.
rows.anchor: المراودة : مفاعلة ، من راد يرود إذا جاء وذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doors she locked are said to have numbered seven.
rows.anchor: قيل : كانت سبعة . وقرىء : ( هيت )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hayta has several readings and forms; hāʾ may be open or closed, and hīʾtu can mean I am ready, from hāʾa yahīʾu; the lām attaches to the verb, while with an exclamation it clarifies the addressee.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( هيت ) بفتح الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿādh Allāh means I seek refuge in God.
rows.anchor: معاذ الله } أعوذ بالله معاذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabbī means my master and owner, Qitfir; Joseph recalls the Aziz's instruction to honor him and refuses to repay that hospitality by betraying his household.
rows.anchor: سيدي ومالكي ، يريد قطفير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers who do not prosper are those who repay good with evil; alternatively, the phrase means adulterers who wrong themselves, or God as the one who causes outcomes.
rows.anchor: الذين يجازون الحسن بالسيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamma means to intend or resolve; the cited line about intending but not acting supports its sense, as does the noun hammām for one who carries intentions through.
rows.anchor: هم بالأمر إذا قصده وعزم عليه ، قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's hamma is an inclination toward intimacy under youthful desire, not a resolved sinful intention; restraining a severe temptation merits praise, and a firm resolve would conflict with God's calling him sincere.
rows.anchor: أن نفسه مالت إلى المخالطة ونازعت إليها عن شهوة الشباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to lawlā is omitted and supplied as: had Joseph not seen his Lord's proof, he would have consummated the intimacy; the wording itself indicates the deleted result.
rows.anchor: جوابه محذوف ، تقديره : لولا أن رأى برهان ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, hamma bihā means he came close to intending it, as in saying I would have killed him had I not feared God, meaning nearly did so.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد بقوله : { وهم بها } وشارف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may remain under the oath introduced by laqad, or be treated as a new sentence; on the latter reading pause after she intended, which signals a difference between the two intentions.
rows.anchor: الأمران جائزان . ومن حق القارىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawlā cannot have its result advanced because it is conditional and conditions begin the clause; omission is allowed when context supplies the result.
rows.anchor: لأن لولا لا يتقدم عليها جوابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although intercourse requires two people, the verse presents the intentions separately and must not erase that distinction: she sought her gratification and he nearly sought his, but the proof stopped him.
rows.anchor: قد جاء بالهمين على سبيل التفصيل حيث قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istabaqā al-bāb means they raced to the door, either with a deleted preposition or with istabaqā carrying the sense of rushing toward it; Joseph fled while she pursued to stop him.
rows.anchor: وتسابقا إلى الباب على حذف الجار وإيصال الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though she had locked the doors, this was the outer exit; Kaʿb reports that the lock pins fell one by one as Joseph escaped.
rows.anchor: أراد الباب البراني الذي هو المخرج من الدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaddat from the rear means she pulled his shirt from behind and tore it as he fled and she followed to prevent his escape.
rows.anchor: اجتذبته من خلفه فانقد ، أي انشق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They found her husband Qitfir; a wife calls her husband sayyid. One view says Yusuf is not included in their master because he was not truly his legal slave.
rows.anchor: وصادفا بعلها وهو قطفير ، تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The husband was either coming in or seated with the woman's cousin when the pair met him.
rows.anchor: ألفياه مقبلا يريد أن يدخل . وقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She devised a tactic to clear herself and punish Joseph while frightening him into compliance after he refused willingly, as her later threat confirms.
rows.anchor: جاءت بحيلة جمعت فيها غرضيها : وهما تبرئة ساحتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In her accusation, mā may be negative, saying jail is his sole punishment, or interrogative, asking what penalty he deserves besides jail.
rows.anchor: نافية ، أي : ليس جزاؤه إلا السجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She avoids naming Joseph to make the charge general, claiming anyone who wrongs the Aziz's household deserves prison or torment, which heightens her threat.
rows.anchor: قصدت العموم ، وأن كل من أراد بأهلك سوءا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The painful punishment is said to be whipping.
rows.anchor: وقيل : العذاب الأليم الضرب بالسياط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph had to defend himself after her accusation and therefore truthfully says she tried to seduce him; otherwise he would have concealed it.
rows.anchor: ولما أغرت به وعرضته للسجن والعذاب وجب عليه الدفع عن نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witness may be her cousin, the man at the door, a wise adviser to the king, or a family member who saw what happened; God moved a relative to defend Joseph and uphold truth.
rows.anchor: قيل كان ابن عم لها ، إنما ألقى الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says four infants spoke: Pharaoh's hairdresser's son, Joseph's witness, Jurayj's companion, and Jesus.
rows.anchor: تكلم أربعة وهم صغار : ابن ماشطة فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witness's statement is called testimony because it functioned as evidence establishing Joseph's claim and invalidating hers.
rows.anchor: لما أدى مؤدي الشهادة في أن ثبت به قول يوسف وبطل قولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional sentence can follow the verb witnessed because it is quoted speech or an implied statement by the witness.
rows.anchor: لأنها قول من القول ، أو على إرادة القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A front tear supports her claim because she could tear his shirt while defending herself, or because he rushed after her and tripped on the front of his garment; a rear tear proves she pursued him.
rows.anchor: إذا كان تابعها وهي دافعته عن نفسها قدت قميصه من قدامه بالدفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings min qablu and min duburu use ḍamma as directional adverbs; indefinite form means a side called front or rear, while Ibn Abī Isḥāq's fatḥa makes the two directions proper feminine names, and both may have a silent ʿayn.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( من قبل ) ومن دبر ، بالضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A future conditional with past kāna means if it is established that the shirt was cut, like promising repayment for a prior favor if someone later claims it.
rows.anchor: لأن المعنى أنه يعلم أن كان قميصه قد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Qitfir saw the shirt cut from behind, he knew Joseph was innocent and his wife was lying.
rows.anchor: يعني قطفير وعلم براءة يوسف وصدقه وكذبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her scheme may refer to her accusation or her desire for Joseph; the address to women generalizes from her to her sex, whose subtle, effective plotting can outmaneuver men.
rows.anchor: الخطاب لها ولأمتها . وإنما استعظم كيد النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars say they fear women more than Satan, since God calls Satan's scheme weak but calls women's scheme great.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض العلماء : أنا أخاف من النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yūsuf omits the vocative particle because he is nearby and attentive, which brings him close and softens the address.
rows.anchor: حذف منه حرف النداء لأنه منادى قريب مفاطن للحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz tells Joseph to conceal the matter and his wife to seek forgiveness; al-khāṭiʾīn denotes deliberate sinners, using the masculine plural generically for the feminine.
rows.anchor: الأمر واكتمه ولا تحدث به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz was a gentle man, and a report says he was not jealous.
rows.anchor: وما كان العزيز إلا رجلا حليما . وروي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women in the city were five: the wives of the cupbearer, baker, animal keeper, prison keeper, and chamberlain.
rows.anchor: وكن خمسا : امرأة الساقي ، وامرأة الخباز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Niswa is a singular collective for women; its grammatical gender is nonliteral, so the verb lacks a feminine marker, and the noun has dialects with nūn kasra or ḍamma.
rows.anchor: والنسوة اسم مفرد لجمع المرأة وتأنيثه غير حقيقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-madīna is Egypt; the Aziz means the king in Arabic; fatā means her male servant, with fatātī for a female servant.
rows.anchor: في مصر { قال ما } يردن قطفير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaghafah means his love pierced the heart's covering and reached its core; shighāf is the heart's covering or a thin layer called its tongue.
rows.anchor: خرق حبه شغاف قلبها حتى وصل إلى الفؤاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha's line uses shighāf for the heart's membrane, supporting that lexical meaning.
rows.anchor:
قال النابغة :
وقد حال هم دون ذلك والج … مكان الشغاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with ʿayn, shaʿafahā, comes from scorching a camel with tar; a cited line uses the same root for the burning treatment.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( شعفها ) بالعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥubban is an accusative of specification, and fī ḍalālin mubīn means plainly mistaken and far from the right path.
rows.anchor: في خطأ وبعد عن طريق الصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their makr is gossip and malicious talk that she loved her Canaanite servant; gossip is called plotting because it occurs secretly in someone's absence.
rows.anchor: باغتيابهن وسوء قالتهن ، وقولهن : امرأة العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, she had entrusted them with her secret and they disclosed it.
rows.anchor: كانت استكتمتهن سرها فأفشينه عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arsalat ilayhin means she invited the women; one report says she invited forty, including the five named.
rows.anchor: دعتهن . قيل : دعت أربعين امرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She prepared cushions and knives so the women would be dazzled and distracted by Joseph and cut themselves reflexively; perhaps she also intended to shame them and frighten Joseph with a group holding knives.
rows.anchor: ما يتكئن عليه من نمارق ، قصدت بتلك الهيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muttakaʾ may mean a couch for meals, drinking, and conversation, as wealthy people reclined.
rows.anchor: جلس طعام لأنهم كانوا يتكؤن للطعام والشراب والحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A transmitted saying forbids a man from eating while reclining.
rows.anchor: نهى أن يأكل الرجل متكئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, muttakaʾ means food by euphemism: to say people leaned at someone’s home means they feasted there, and cushions were prepared for guests.
rows.anchor: وقيل : { * متكأ } طعاما ، من قولك اتكأنا عند فلان : طمعنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jamīl's verse uses اتكأنا to mean feasting, illustrating the food interpretation of muttakaʾ.
rows.anchor: فظللنا بنعمة واتكأنا … وشربنا الحلال من قلله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid explains muttakaʾ as food cut with a knife; the cutter presses against what is being cut.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد { * متكأ } طعاما يحز حزا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings include mutkan without hamza and al-Ḥasan's elongated mutkāʾ, an expanded vowel analogous to other lengthened forms.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( متكا ) بغير همز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading means citron, supported by a poem about gifting mutka; other reports identify the prepared food as citron, bananas, and watermelon, or as things to cut, from a verb meaning to sever.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( متكأ ) وهو الأترج

rows.speaker: الأعرج
rows.claim: Al-Aʿraj reads mutkaʾ as a verbal noun from takaʾa, to lean.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج : { * متكأ } مفعلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akbarnahu means they found Joseph magnificent and were awed by his striking beauty.
rows.anchor: أعظمنه وهبن ذلك الحسن الرائع والجمال الفائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's beauty is compared to the full moon; a Prophetic report says the Prophet saw him on the Night Journey and described him as the full moon.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 543 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports say Joseph's face shone on Egypt's walls, that no one could describe him, that he resembled Adam at creation, or inherited beauty from Sarah.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان يوسف إذا سار في أزقة مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akbarnahu can also mean the women menstruated, with hāʾ as a pause marker; menstruation was called becoming adult, and Abū al-Ṭayyib's verse reflects this reading.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أكبرن بمعنى حضن ، والهاء للسكت
